newsitem.title: ROMANIA: SOCCER-STEAUA ACCUSE GALATASARAY OVER FILIPESCU DEAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STEAUA ACCUSE GALATASARAY OVER FILIPESCU DEAL.

text.p: Romanian champions Steaua Bucharest have accused Galatasaray of Turkey of illegally poaching midfielder Iulian Filipescu by excluding them from contract negotiations.
Filipescu signed for Galatasaray last month. He travelled to Turkey on Thursday and was immediately presented to local reporters and fans.
But Steaua claim the deal is invalid and said they had returned to Galatasaray a cheque for $800,000 -- the first instalment of the transfer fee -- with a letter of complaint.

"The Turkish club is in the wrong because it began talks with Filipescu and left Steaua out of them," marketing director Constantin Matei said. "They didn't inform us in writing according to FIFA and UEFA rules."
He said the midfielder was contracted to Steaua until 1999.

But Filipescu's agent Ioan Becali said his client was free to move under his current contract provided Steaua received $800,000 during his first year with his new club, $1 million in the second and $1.2 million in the third.
"Galatasaray are ready to pay these sums so the transfer deal is perfectly valid," Becali said.
The former European Cup winners said Filipescu, who played in Steaua's 1-0 Champions' League win over Poland's Widzew Lodz on Wednesday, faces a ban unless he returns to the club.
"Iulian Filipescu must return immediately to Steaua Bucharest if he wishes to avoid a delicate situation," the club's letter to Galatasaray read.
